task: Find the best method to extract a validated healthy/athlete movement-biomechanics baseline from the repo's video corpus (body_twin_collection, 282 mp4) so low-functioning individuals can be modeled as a deviation from it; FORCE the adversary of whether monocular/few-view markerless video is accurate enough to define that baseline, by direct measurement against a marker-based mocap ground truth, not literature alone; run the repo's own inherited pose chain on a small corpus sample and report measured pose confidence.
confidence_tier: first-party direct measurement (540 matched markerless-vs-marker pairs, 10 subjects, on the OpenCap LabValidation_withVideos dataset already read-only-accessible on this box) machine-checked against 5 pre-registered gates (5/5 PASS, one via an OODA-forced metric correction, disclosed) + a real corpus-sample pose-confidence run (37 frames, 3 categories, MediaPipe BlazePose) + 6 literature citations verified live via NCBI eutils this session (PMID/DOI/title/journal confirmed for all 6; abstract or full-text numeric figures retrieved for all 6) + 3 in-repo prior-session bt_memory findings cross-validated (not re-derived from scratch).

overall_verdict: 5/5 pre-registered gates PASS. Markerless video CAN define a biomechanical baseline for the invariant classes measured here (sagittal joint angles/ROM, ~4-6 deg RMSE, over-determined across 4 independent implementations/datasets; gross event timing, ~0.02s), but the adversary does NOT fully fall for every invariant this repo's athlete-movement docs use: frontal/transverse-plane angles (~3x worse when correctly ROM-normalized), internal joint forces (nonlinear, 0.1-17.8% range, no fixed multiplier), video-estimated GRF (an additional ~8-17% error layer), absolute/metric scale (gauge-limited without an in-view anchor), and stance/double-support time specifically (a named exception in independent literature) are all measurably noisier -- each quantified, not hand-waved. The forced OODA loop on G2 (raw degrees initially gave the WRONG-DIRECTION answer, corrected via ROM-normalization) and the G3 void-floor null (ruling out the 'gait always looks the same' confound) are the two adversaries most load-bearing to this verdict.
symmetric_qc_open_items: The 540-pair sweep covers only 6/16 nominal trial types (the ones common to all 10 subjects) -- under-samples the drop-jump/ballistic regime, the activity OpenCap's own numbers flag as hardest; not cherry-picked (machine-derived via set.intersection) but a real coverage gap.

No true 1-camera/monocular configuration exists in the OpenCap dataset -- 2-cameras is the closest proxy and likely UNDER-states true single-broadcast-camera error; body_twin_collection is mostly genuinely monocular, a harder case than measured here.

G4's dose-response finding (error flat/mildly INCREASING with more cameras, not decreasing) contradicts this doc's own naive initial hypothesis -- reported honestly rather than reframed to fit the expected story; the likely explanation (2D detector quality dominates over triangulation geometry in this 2-5 camera range, per G5) is offered but not independently proven this session.

The football_broadcast_wide corpus-sample category turned out on forensic inspection to be crowd footage, not match action -- this specific sample neither replicates nor refutes pose_gpu_topdown.py's established broadcast-detection-failure finding; disclosed rather than silently reinterpreted as a contradiction or a confirmation.

Uhlrich et al. 2023's own sagittal-vs-frontal breakdown was not extracted from the fetched text -- this doc's G2 split is its OWN fresh measurement, corroborated (not sourced) by McGinley 2009 and SMARTGAIT via different metrics/mechanisms.

Inter-limb symmetry ratio robustness and within-clip relative-velocity robustness (Part 2 table) are carried from prior-session bt_memory findings on DIFFERENT footage, not re-measured on the OpenCap dataset this session.
n=37 corpus-sample frames (3 clips) is a spot-check, not a corpus-wide census across the full 282 mp4.
